eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to a peak of 33–35°C in Chengdu on June 3 because early-June climatology and short-range model guidance place the city’s typical daily maximum in the low-to-mid 30s as the monsoon transition brings warmer, more humid air masses. Official long-term averages show June highs of 28–33°C, with occasional excursions to 35–36°C when subtropical ridges strengthen; recent forecast runs from multiple agencies converge on 34–36°C under mostly sunny conditions before afternoon convection develops. Differentiation between 33°C, 34°C, and 35°C hinges on exact timing of cloud cover, boundary-layer moisture, and any late-day showers that could cap the afternoon maximum by 1–2°C. With the market tightly bunched and resolution occurring in under 24 hours, the next updated model suite and real-time surface observations will determine which of these three outcomes captures the greatest share of trader capital.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current National Weather Service guidance and ensemble forecasts point to a high near 73–79°F in Los Angeles on June 4, with the marine layer and persistent onshore flow expected to limit afternoon warming at coastal stations such as KLAX. Weak upper-level troughing and normal early-June heights near 586 dam support only modest diurnal heating, while sea-breeze timing and low-cloud coverage introduce the main uncertainty between the 70–71°F and 72–73°F brackets. Updated model runs and the next NWS Area Forecast Discussion will clarify whether the boundary layer mixes deeply enough to push readings into the mid-70s.

Recent observations show temperatures holding in the 35–37°C range without the extreme heatwave spikes seen in May, supporting trader emphasis on the 35°C outcome as the modal result while leaving room for 34°C or 37°C+ depending on the precise timing of peak heating and any minor steering changes. eventMetadata.context_description: Current PAGASA forecasts for Metro Manila point to a June 4 high near 32°C under the early influence of the southwest monsoon, which typically brings increased cloud cover, humidity, and scattered afternoon showers that limit peak heating. Historical June averages hover at 32°C, with daily highs rarely exceeding 34–35°C absent unusual clear-sky conditions. Trader consensus clustering on 32–33°C reflects this climatological baseline and short-range model agreement, though modest uncertainty remains from exact monsoon timing and localized convective activity that can shave or add a degree to the daily maximum.
